TRY: Review data storage

Data storage is elemental to a website's operation. Viewing a web page doesn't involve disk storage, and the webpage's source code isn't saved. Instead, it is retrieved from a web server through web requests on each iteration. Go to <Markup> for viewing source code.

Data from one web page is sometimes needed for concurrent web pages. While a server can save the needed data, doing so is inefficient and adds unnecessary upkeep and maintenance of the server. The browser offers the developer 'localStorage' for this use case.

Go to <GUIDE: Dev Application> for a bit on local storage.

Browser's local storage is domain-based. That means dev tools will report data for each domain holding data. On the home page, https://randomwebbits.com, the To-Do list stores each to-do in a local storage key called `ToDos`. Also, the Dictionary Term component stores words cached as JSON objects to save all the previously searched words.
